steps: Confirm the location
Freestanding room heater only: not in a fireplace and not in a sleeping room. Check with local building or fire officials about restrictions and inspection.

Install as a freestanding space heater with the listed clearances. Never in any fireplace, and never in a bedroom or any area used for sleeping. The stove is certified for insulated, habitable rooms, not a concrete, uninsulated basement or a shop/garage, where constant over-firing can void the warranty (p. 16).

Consult the authority having jurisdiction before installation about the need for a permit (p. 1).
Set clearances
Lay out residential, alcove or mobile-home clearances from the p. 8 table and drawing. Alcove and mobile home need double-wall pipe; Canada needs 18" from single-wall pipe.
Floor protection

On a combustible floor, fit a non-combustible UL 1618-2009 (Type 1) shield: in the USA 16" out in front and 8" each side of the loading door, at least 31.75" x 37.5", plus 2" either side under the connector.
Combustion air
Balance intake air against HRVs, air handlers, range hoods and dryers. With outside air at the rear, keep its outside termination no higher than the rear connection.

In air-tight homes, make sure there is enough intake (combustion) air for every exhausting appliance: HRV systems, constantly running air-handler fans, fireplaces, range hoods, dryers. If outside air connects directly to the stove's rear, keep the fresh-air pipe's outside termination no higher than the rear connection, or flue gases may reverse through the intake. Consult an HVAC specialist.
Connector & chimney
6" 24 MSG steel connector to a UL-103HT / CAN/ULC-S629 or lined masonry chimney; screw every joint; support package at ceilings, listed thimble through combustible walls.
Chimney height
15 ft minimum recommended, stove top to termination, up to 1000 ft; add for altitude, elbows, "T" sections and horizontal runs. No more than one offset.
Fan power (if fitted)
Plug the fan kit's three-prong grounded plug straight into a grounded receptacle. Never cut the grounding prong; don't route the cord in front of or under the stove.
Mobile home extras
Outside air required (fitting the hose first is recommended); double-wall close-clearance pipe; roof exit only; fasten the pedestal base to the floor with a #10 screw and washer.
Hang the door; fan kit
Seat the door on the bottom hinge pin, then the top; lower until the hinge surfaces meet. Install the S.Z6814 fan kit per its own instructions.

1. Align the bottom door hinge hole with the bottom firebox hinge pin. The door is heavy; hold it firmly.
  2. Lower the door onto the bottom hinge pin, then align the top door hinge hole with the top firebox hinge pin.
  3. Lower the door onto the pins until the door hinge surface contacts the firebox hinge surface.
Never operate the stove with the loading door off or left open. It can lead to a run-away fire.
Hand over
Complete the installer details on the last page and leave the manual with the homeowner.

The installer notes ask for: dealer name and address, installer name, signature and phone number, date installed, and the appliance serial number. The warranty also asks the owner to mail the warranty registration card (p. 43); the cards come in the manual kit.

Thermostat set too high → lower it

Obstruction in chimney or cap → clean, remove it
Faulty thermometer → check its calibration

items: Spark arrestor screen plugged → clean to bare metal wire

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
The first fire cures the paint: expect a strong smell, some smoke and a color change. Burn low for several hours with a door or window open.

  1. Check the firebricks are all in place. Build the fire on the bottom brick. No grate.
  2. Thermostat to HIGH. Fan (if fitted) off.
  3. Open the bypass, then the loading door.
  4. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper at the front. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, with air gaps.
  5. Light it and leave the door cracked open. Stay with the stove.
  6. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  7. Latch the door. As the combustor temperature climbs, close the bypass and turn fans on high (if fitted).
  8. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads Active, open the bypass and door. Finish loading, as far back as you can. Latch the door and close the bypass.
  9. Stay on HIGH until the fire is well established: at least 500F, needle in the Active zone.
  10. Turn the thermostat down gradually. Too low, too fast, and the fire may go out or the combustor may stop working. If so, turn it back up.
  11. Turn the fan (if fitted) on after the initial warm-up.
Note: steps 7 and 11 on p. 20 give two different times to switch the fan on, and p. 16 says to keep fans off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Check the thermometer first. If the needle has dropped into the Inactive zone, start again with "Light a fire." If it's still Active:

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to HIGH and wait a few minutes for the air flow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass door and wait a few more minutes.
  3. With the bypass open, crack the loading door to let room air into the firebox. Give it a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and reload. If a lot of smoke spills out, close the door slightly until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Stay on HIGH until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down.

Don't be afraid to fill it: the wood only burns at the rate the thermostat is set. Load only inside the usable loading area, which the manual shows as a diagram on p. 19, and never build the fire close to the glass. On low settings you may see little flame. If the needle stays Active, the burn is continuing.

Mild spring and fall days

On milder days (the manual suggests about 55F to 70F), run it on HIGH for 30 minutes after lighting and reloading, then turn it down gradually. Too warm? Burn smaller loads instead of turning the thermostat lower.

control.title: Thermostat, bypass door & fan
control.html:
Thermostat

The knob is at the upper right rear corner. HIGH gives the most heat. Turn it counter clockwise for less. Make changes gradually, because a sudden change can make the thermostat work improperly. The low end has a factory-set minimum burn rate, and altering it is against federal regulations. The tested low-burn setting is shown as a figure on p. 22.

Bypass door

The bypass door is inside the dome at the top of the firebox. Opening it lets smoke skip the combustor. You open it to light, to reload and before the chimney is swept. Use the bypass handle: hook the side of the latch and pull the rod out to open; push on the center of the latch to close.

Never touch the bypass latch by hand. It can cause serious burns. A bypass left open too long can also cause a run-away fire.

Fan (optional kit)

About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match the fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

Note: the manual gives three answers on when to switch the fan on. Step 7 on p. 20 says turn fans on high when you close the bypass; step 11 on p. 20 says turn the fan on after the initial warm-up; p. 16 says keep fans off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature.

thermometer.title: Reading the catalytic thermometer
thermometer.html:
The thermometer on top of the stove reads the exhaust after it passes through the catalytic combustor. It tells you whether the combustor is working. Keep the stove running in the Active zone.

Activeabove 500F · combustor working
Inactivebelow 500F · not producing a clean burn

Turn the fan off for a while before you read it.

Note: the manual gives two times for how long the fan should be off before you read the thermometer: about 5 minutes on p. 18 and 10 minutes on pp. 29 and 36.

Turning the thermostat down, especially early in a burn, can make the combustor temperature climb for up to several hours. That's normal.

Test the combustor

  1. Light a fire as usual and let it burn, well established, for 1 hour.
  2. Set the thermostat to a medium-low burn rate.
  3. After 5 minutes, check the needle. Active means the combustor is working.
  4. Repeat for at least 3 burn cycles.
  5. Still Inactive? The combustor may need cleaning. If cleaning doesn't help, it may need replacing. Ask your Blaze King dealer.

The thermometer itself can be faulty too, so have it checked before blaming the combustor.

wood.title: Choosing firewood
wood.html:
Burn cord wood only, at 20% moisture or lower. That means wood split, stacked so air reaches it, and covered from rain and snow for at least 24 months. Hardwood and softwood both burn well. Dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and keep them indoors for 24 hours.
  2. Split each one down the middle.
  3. Measure the split face at three points, 2" from each end and in the middle, with the pins in line with the grain.
  4. Average all the readings.

Never burn

  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood. It can cause excessive creosote build-up, and if that ignites it can cause a chimney fire that may result in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
  • Salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the stove and voids the warranty.
  • Treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Lots of offcuts, pressed logs or small, very dry pieces. Used in excess they can overheat and damage the firebox.
Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire in the stove. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm. Keep all such liquids away from the stove while it is in use.

glass.title: Keeping the glass clean
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to burn on high for a while after each reload. Moisture driven out of fresh wood causes much of the creosote on the glass. Before an overnight low burn, leave the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour.

Long stretches on a very low setting leave creosote on the glass. Run the stove on HIGH for about 30 minutes to burn most of it off.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool. Never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth. No abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse well with water after any cleaner. Leftover cleaner bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door. Don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. Replacement glass must be 5mm ceramic glass.

The warranty covers thermal breakage only. It doesn't cover glass that was struck, contaminated or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners.

care.title: Ashes & routine care
care.html:
Do all maintenance with the fire out and the stove cool. The glass and surfaces stay hot long after the fire is out.

Ashes

Remove ashes whenever they come within one inch of the door opening, but leave a bed about 1/2" thick. Wood burns best on it. Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a noncombustible floor or the ground outside, away from anything combustible, until every cinder has cooled.

Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases.

Through the season

  • Look over the combustor at least three times a season. Clean its face with a soft paint brush or a vacuum held near it (lift off the flame shield first). Never scrape it.
  • Paper-test the door gasket: latch the door on a dollar bill and pull. No resistance means the door needs adjusting.
  • Clean the thermometer probe and check its calibration.
  • Check the fan for ash, dust, pet dander and lint at the start of each burn season.
  • Clean out and inspect the stove at the end of every season.
Note: p. 29 gives steps to clean and calibrate the thermometer, then says any thermostat or thermometer maintenance must be done by a certified installer.

chimney.title: Chimney care & creosote
chimney.html:
A slow fire gives off tar and other vapors. In the cooler chimney they condense with moisture into creosote, which can ignite and burn extremely hot. The hotter the fire, the less creosote builds up.

  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season until you know how often they need cleaning.
  • Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass door before the chimney is swept, so soot and creosote fall into the firebox.
  • A damaged chimney section must be replaced.

What leads to a run-away or chimney fire

  • Wrong fuel, or small pieces you'd normally use as kindling
  • Leaving the loading door ajar too long
  • Worn or badly installed gaskets
  • Creosote in the chimney
  • Leaving the bypass door open too long

In extremely cold weather, the water vapor from the chimney can freeze and block it. Burn on HIGH for 5 to 10 minutes to melt any ice.

safety.title: Safety & chimney fires
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and other combustibles at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood in the clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Have at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows.
  • Run it only with the door closed, the gasket in good shape, and the combustor and flame shield in place.
If a smoke or CO alarm sounds, get everyone out of the house right away.

If the chimney catches fire

  1. Turn the thermostat fully counter clockwise. Make sure the loading door and bypass door are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. Use an extinguisher or a garden hose if needed.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're sure the chimney isn't damaged. Have a certified chimney sweep inspect the chimney and flue connector.

Damage from a chimney fire isn't covered by the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
For the original purchaser of a stove bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It starts on the purchase date and can't be transferred.

All parts, materials, paint finish1 year, parts + limited labor
Fan assemblies, modular thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years, parts + limited labor
Steel firebox components5 years, parts
Catalytic combustor6 years
Maker's brochure: 10-year extended warranty on the catalytic combustor.

For parts covered beyond the first year, you pay a share of the then-current retail cost: 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4, 80% in year 5. The combustor has its own scale: no charge for the first three years, then 60%, 70% and 80% in years 4, 5 and 6.

Not covered

  • Gaskets and firebrick; normal wear such as paint discoloration
  • Over-firing (warped plates, burnt-off paint), salt-saturated or treated wood, misuse
  • Chimney-fire and transit damage; draft problems from the surroundings
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of noticing it, with proof of purchase. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

Certified to the 2020 EPA particulate emission standards using crib wood (EPA test method 28R). Tested and listed to UL 1482-11 (R2022) and CAN/ULC-S627:2023. The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered, and operating with the catalytic combustor deactivated or removed is against federal regulations.

Build the fire directly on the firebrick; no grate. Load fuel only in the usable loading area, shown as a shaded diagram on p. 19. Overall appliance dimensions are given only on the drawing on p. 7.

specFlue.title: Flue connector & chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D. (152 mm)
Flue pipe6" diameter, 24 MSG steel; no aluminum or galvanized
Chimney (USA)listed factory-built, UL-103HT
Chimney (Canada)listed factory-built, CAN/ULC-S629
Orcode-approved masonry chimney with a flue liner
  • Mobile home and residential close-clearance installs need a 6" listed double-wall, close-clearance connector with a matching listed factory-built chimney.
  • Don't connect to a chimney serving another appliance, or to air distribution ductwork.
  • A chimney connector is required; don't install the chimney directly at the outlet. Keep the run as direct as possible and fasten every joint with sheet metal screws.
  • Never pass flue pipe through an attic, roof space, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling. Use a chimney support package at a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall.
  • Prefab chimney: buy all components from the same chimney manufacturer. Masonry chimney: have it inspected by a certified professional (no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage) and cleaned before installing.
  • Chimney at least 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above any roof or obstruction within 10 ft.
  • Recommended: double-wall pipe from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box; 3 ft vertical from stove top to elbow on wall exits; a pair of 45 degree elbows rather than one 90; a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, in a masonry chimney.

specHeight.title: Recommended chimney height
specHeight.html:
Blaze King recommends at least 15 ft of vertical chimney, stove top to termination, from sea level up to 1000 ft. Required regardless: 3 ft above the highest point where it passes through the roof, and 2 ft above the highest part of the roof or any obstruction within 10 ft (measured horizontally).

Minimum height by elevation · elbows 0 / 2 X 15° / 2 X 30° / 2 X 45°

0 - 1000 ft15 / 16 / 18 / 19 ft
1000 - 2000 ft15.5 / 16.5 / 18.5 / 19.5 ft
2000 - 3000 ft16 / 17 / 19 / 20 ft
3000 - 4000 ft16.5 / 17.5 / 19.5 / 20.5 ft
4000 - 5000 ft17 / 18 / 20 / 21 ft
5000 - 6000 ft17.5 / 18.5 / 20.5 / 21.5 ft
6000 - 7000 ft18 / 19 / 21 / 22 ft
7000 - 8000 ft18.5 / 19.5 / 21.5 / 22.5 ft

No more than one offset (two elbows). Add for other components: 90° elbow = 2.0 ft; "T" section = 3.0 ft; 1.0 ft of horizontal run = 2 ft of vertical rise. Sea-level example from the manual: 15.0 ft + one 90° elbow 2.0 ft + 2.0' horizontal run 4.0 ft + one base "T" 3.0 ft = 24.0 ft. Guidelines only; see Draft Performance (p. 9).

Note: the 90° elbow allowance reads two ways on p. 12. The table lists 19 ft with two 45° elbows against 15 ft with none (0 - 1000 ft) and notes that two 45° elbows equal one 90° elbow, while the component list on the same page adds only 2.0 ft for a 90° elbow.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required. On a combustible floor, a non-combustible floor shield must be used.

USA, out from the front16"
USA, out from either side of the loading door8"
Minimum size, USA31.75" x 37.5" (807 mm x 953 mm)
Minimum size, Canada37" x 47.5" (940 mm x 1207 mm)
ListingUL 1618-2009 (Type 1); no insulation value needed

Canada (CSA B365): a continuous, durable, non-combustible ember pad at least 18" (450 mm) beyond any side with a door, running the full width plus 8" (200 mm) each side, and at least 8" (200 mm) beyond the other sides. Less than 8" from a wall, the pad need only reach the base of the wall. Not on carpet unless structurally supported.

A non-combustible shield is also required under the chimney connector, at least 2" either side of it. Blaze King doesn't recommend adhesive-based vinyl flooring in front of the stove (it can warp permanently).

specMobile.title: Mobile home & transportable building
specMobile.html:
• Approved for mobile homes (USA) and transportable buildings (Canada); roof exit only.
  • Outside air is required. Installing the outside-air hose (flexible metal tube, not supplied) and its termination before the stove is recommended. Keep it open at all times. Its wall termination must never be higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove.
  • Flue pipe must be double-wall, close-clearance type with CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610 designation; single-wall is not allowed. Insulated chimney: listed factory-built, CAN/ULC-S629 or UL-103HT. Buy the ceiling support package from the chimney manufacturer.
  • Fasten the stove to the floor with a #10 screw and washer through the hole in the pedestal base (p. 14).
  • The chimney must be removed to transport the building.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, wall and roof. Never install in a bedroom or sleeping area.

Figure labels on pp. 4, 7, 8 and 22 use a different glyph scramble (e.g. 'whhC hw t![[', 'ϯϭ Ϯ', 'ϲϱΣ') that the 29 rule does not decode, so they were not used: the appliance dimension drawing (p. 7, so overall height/width/depth are not in the guide), the clearance drawing labels and the *1 / *2 / *3 footnotes (pp. 4, 8), and the tested low-burn knob position (p. 22). Clearance letters A-H and I-M are defined only in the p. 8 drawing; the guide gives the printed letter values and points to the drawing. Alcove row: the extracted text doesn't show which two columns are n/a (probably E and F, since the last two values match residential G/H), so the guide lists the six values in printed order. Metric conversions differ slightly for the same inch values (K = 16" is 407 mm on p. 4 vs 406 mm on p. 8; 18" is 458 mm on p. 4, 456 mm on p. 8, 457 mm for I and 450 mm in the p. 8 text); the guide uses inches only for those. Usable firebox loading area is a shaded diagram only (p. 19). Warranty: the p. 40 coverage grid is a check-mark table, so the drawer uses the prose terms on pp. 41-43; the combustor's 6-year cost scale (p. 41) and the beyond-first-year scale of 20/40/60/80% (p. 43, item 24, framed as the five-year warranty) are shown as separate schedules. The manual says to check draft with a manometer against manufacturer specifications and refers to a 'CHIMNEY DRAFTS'/'DRAFTS' section, but gives no draft value. Combustor part numbers: OEM 115-1505-C2 (pp. 4, 26) vs parts list S.CAT14 'Combustor Assembly' (p. 38); not shown in the guide. Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: heating area, maximum burn time, overall height, the convection deck for the fan kit, and the product-page '1 inch at rear and corners' (manual has B = 1" and E = 1" but doesn't say which sides they are). Catalog weight 258 lb matches the manual's shipping weight. The bilingual label text on p. 4 duplicates the English; nothing French-only needed translating.
